bull.b: Very low leverage limits financial risk and gives dLocal flexibility to invest in technology, market expansion and product development. Strong returns on equity also indicate that the company is using its capital efficiently.

High retention and expanding merchant share-of-wallet support recurring volume growth and strengthen customer relationships. This suggests dLocal is becoming more deeply embedded in merchant payment workflows across emerging markets.

Rapid payment-volume growth, higher gross profit and raised guidance demonstrate strong demand for dLocal’s emerging-market payment infrastructure. Improving operating leverage and planned automation could support durable earnings growth as scale increases.

bear.b: The multi-year decline in gross and net margins indicates that growth has not translated fully into profitability. Continued pressure from pricing, payment mix or market expansion costs could constrain earnings quality even while revenue grows.

A rising mix of lower-priced flows and volatility in regional spreads can reduce monetization of each payment dollar. Managing processing costs and preserving economics across diverse markets remains a continuing challenge to margin sustainability.

Recent cash generation is strong and closely aligned with earnings, but the prior negative-cash-flow year shows that working capital or payment timing can materially affect conversion. This volatility reduces confidence in the consistency of internally funded growth.
